elements.quote: Trial registration: Not applicable. This systematic review was not prospectively registered.
elements.reason: The abstract explicitly identifies the report as a systematic review.

elements.quote: We evaluated randomized evidence for pain-control strategies during blind outpatient or office-based endometrial biopsy or sampling.
elements.reason: The abstract states the main objective/review question explicitly.

elements.quote: we restricted meta-analysis to randomized comparisons against placebo, saline, placebo gel, distilled water, or other inert controls, defined as controls without intended analgesic activity, that reported extractable intraprocedural pain scores on a 0-10 compatible scale
elements.reason: Key inclusion criteria (design, comparator, outcome) are specified in the abstract.

elements.quote: We searched PubMed, CENTRAL, Embase, Web of Science, Scopus, Wanfang, VIP, ClinicalTrials.gov, and WHO ICTRP from inception to 9 May 2026, with update checks of PubMed and ClinicalTrials.gov on 12 June 2026.
elements.reason: Information sources and last search/update dates are reported.

elements.quote: Risk of bias was assessed with RoB 2 and certainty with GRADE.
elements.reason: Risk-of-b assessment method is specified in the abstract.

elements.quote: Random-effects mean differences were pooled.
elements.reason: Synthesis/presentation methods are stated in the abstract.

elements.quote: Eight randomized trials involving 944 participants were included in the primary meta-analysis.
elements.reason: Number of studies and participants is reported; study characteristics (interventions, comparators) are described.

elements.quote: Pain-control interventions lowered average pain during biopsy compared with inert controls (mean difference, -1.87 points; 95% confidence interval, -2.52 to -1.22; I-squared = 86.7%).
elements.reason: Results for the main outcome (pain) are reported with study/participant numbers; safety results are also summarized ('Harms were sparsely and inconsistently reported').

elements.quote: mean difference, -1.87 points; 95% confidence interval, -2.52 to -1.22
elements.reason: A meta-analysis was conducted and the summary estimate with 95% CI is reported.

elements.quote: Pain-control interventions lowered average pain during biopsy compared with inert controls
elements.reason: Direction of effect and favored group (intervention vs inert controls) are indicated.

elements.quote: Certainty was low for pain reduction and very low for safety.
elements.reason: The abstract summarizes limitations including low/very low certainty and substantial heterogeneity.

elements.quote: These findings support patient-centered discussion of pain-control options but do not establish any specific agent or intervention class as standard care.
elements.reason: The abstract provides interpretation and implications of the results.
No funding statement appears in the abstract content retrieved (text_3/text_4).

elements.quote: Trial registration: Not applicable. This systematic review was not prospectively registered.
elements.reason: The abstract explicitly addresses registration status, stating the review was not registered.
The retrieved evidence contains no Introduction or rationale text describing the current state of knowledge or uncertainties motivating the review.
No retrieved chunk explains the importance of or need for conducting the review; evidence covers methods, results, and limitations only.

No evidence shows whether prior systematic reviews exist or whether the need for an update/replication is explained with citation of a previous review; the Introduction is not represented in the retrieved evidence.
This is a review of pain-control interventions, so a mechanism description would apply, but no retrieved text describes the proposed mechanism of action of the interventions.
No retrieved evidence indicates consideration of a logic model or hypothesized relationships between intervention components and outcomes.

None of the retrieved evidence contains an explicit statement of the review objective(s) or question(s). The retrieved chunks cover author contributions, abbreviations, methods of screening/extraction, risk of bias, and tables, but no objectives statement from the Introduction or elsewhere.

This is a review of intervention effects (pain-control strategies vs inert controls), so planned comparisons in PICO form would apply, but no PICO-formulated comparison statement appears in the retrieved evidence. Only implicit intervention/comparator details appear in extraction methods (e.g., text_10), not an explicit planned-comparison statement.

elements.quote: Population: women undergoing outpatient or office-based blind endometrial biopsy or endometrial sampling for any clinical indication. Intervention: peri-procedural analgesic, anesthetic, or pain-control strategies... Comparator: placebo, normal saline, placebo gel, distilled water, or another credible inert control... Outcomes: the primary outcome was pain during biopsy or sampling on a 0-10 compatible scale... Study design: randomized controlled trials were eligible for efficacy synthesis
elements.reason: Full PICO framework with population, intervention, comparator, outcomes, and eligible study designs is explicitly specified.

elements.quote: No restrictions were placed on publication year, language, country, indication for biopsy, menopausal status, or biopsy device
elements.reason: Report characteristics (year, language, publication status) are addressed by explicitly stating no restrictions; handling of abstracts, registry entries, and secondary reports is also specified.

elements.quote: reports without usable pain or safety outcomes were excluded from review synthesis
elements.reason: Exclusion categories distinguish records lacking extractable results (e.g., 'no public extractable results', median-only reporting) from those without the outcome measured, but the review does not explicitly separate 'outcome not measured' from 'outcome measured but not reported'.

elements.quote: To avoid mixing clinically different comparisons, we organized the evidence into three tiers. Tier 1 was the prespecified primary meta-analysis. It included inert-controlled randomized comparisons with extractable intra-procedural means and standard deviations. Tier 2 comprised sensitivity analyses... Tier 3 comprised narrative or tabulated contextual evidence.
elements.reason: Synthesis groups (three tiers) are explicitly specified and linked to the comparison types (inert-controlled vs active-comparator, co-intervention, etc.) defined in the objectives.

elements.quote: Studies were excluded from the primary analysis when they centered on hysteroscopy-guided biopsy... because those settings differ in instrumentation, duration, uterine distension, cervical manipulation, and pain mechanisms.
elements.reason: Rationales for notable eligibility restrictions (procedure type, inert comparator requirement, extractable data) are explicitly provided.

elements.quote: Database and register searches covered database inception to 2026-05-09, with Scopus and WHO ICTRP record capture completed on 2026-05-10. ... Additional PubMed and ClinicalTrials.gov update checks were conducted on 2026-06-12
elements.reason: Search dates for each source are explicitly reported, including update-check dates.

elements.quote: The PRISMA-counted search set included PubMed, CENTRAL, Embase, Web of Science Core Collection, Scopus, Wanfang, VIP, ClinicalTrials.gov, and WHO ICTRP. ... Database and register searches covered database inception to 2026-05-09
elements.reason: Database names and coverage (inception to search date) are reported, but no search interfaces/platforms are specified.

elements.quote: ClinicalTrials.gov and WHO ICTRP were searched with simplified procedure and pain-control terms to maximize sensitivity. ChiCTR was checked with manual Chinese and English registry terms
elements.reason: Registers (ClinicalTrials.gov, WHO ICTRP, ChiCTR) are named with search approach; date restrictions covered by inception-to-2026-05-09 statement.
No websites or search engines beyond databases/registers were reported as searched.
No organisations or manufacturers were reported as contacted.
No individuals were reported as contacted to identify studies.
No reference-list searching was reported.
No backward or forward citation searching was reported.
No journals or conference proceedings were hand-searched.

elements.quote: Database-specific syntax, full English and Chinese search strings, record counts, export or capture formats, and update checks are provided in the Supplementary Search Appendix and the repository package.
elements.reason: The full search strategies for each database are not reproduced in the manuscript itself; they are deferred to a supplementary appendix and repository package, so the complete strategies as actually run are not fully presented in the main text.

elements.quote: No date, language, or publication-status filters were applied to the main bibliographic search strategies.
elements.reason: Search limits are described (no date, language, or publication-status filters; database inception to a specified date), but no explicit justification of these limits by reference to the eligibility criteria is provided.
No citation of published search approaches, filters (e.g., Cochrane RCT filter), or descriptions of adaptations is present in the retrieved evidence.
No text-analysis or NLP tools for identifying or refining search terms are reported; machine prescreening mentioned relates to screening, not search-term development.
No tools for translating search strings between databases or sources are described.
No validation of the search strategy (process or validation studies) is reported in the retrieved evidence.
No peer review of the search strategy (e.g., PRESS) is described.

elements.quote: The search strategies combined three concept blocks: the target procedure, the pain-control strategy, and randomized or controlled trial design.
elements.reason: The final conceptual structure of the search (three concept blocks) is explicitly described, covering the conceptual basis of the search design.

elements.quote: Screening and eligibility-critical decisions were checked by rotating reviewer pairs drawn from three reviewers: Bin Yue, Cui Zhao, and Xiaogang Hao. At least two reviewers verified records retained as include, unclear, full-text, or boundary decisions.
elements.reason: The number of reviewers at title/abstract and full-text stages is specified (at least two from a pool of three named reviewers), with two-reviewer checking also reported for full-text exclusions and extraction.

elements.quote: Because the workflow also used machine prescreening, staged human verification, and consensus adjudication, this kappa estimate describes that paired verification subset and should not be interpreted as full independent duplicate screening of all 2,013 title/abstract records.
elements.reason: The authors explicitly state that full independent duplicate screening was not performed for all records; paired verification was used for a subset, so independence at each screening stage is only partially reported.

elements.quote: Disagreements were resolved by discussion, with senior clinical and methodological input from Zhirong Dai when needed.
elements.reason: Disagreement resolution via discussion with senior adjudication input is explicitly described.

elements.quote: Of 208 reports or records sought for retrieval or eligibility clarification, 10 were not retrieved or had no public extractable results and 198 were assessed for eligibility.
elements.reason: Records sought for eligibility clarification are counted, but no process for contacting study investigators to obtain or confirm eligibility information is described.
Although no language restriction was applied to eligibility, no methods for translating non-English abstracts or articles are reported.

elements.quote: Because the workflow also used machine prescreening, staged human verification, and consensus adjudication...
elements.reason: Machine prescreening is acknowledged as part of the workflow, but the automation tools, their configuration, and how they were integrated into the selection process are not described.
No externally derived classifiers are identified or described.
No internally derived classifiers, their training, or validation are described.
No machine-learning prioritisation tools or screening stopping rules are described.
No crowdsourcing platforms are mentioned.
No previously screened datasets used to eliminate records are described.

elements.quote: One reviewer extracted each record and a second reviewer checked eligibility classification, arm denominators, outcome timepoint, mean, standard deviation, direction of effect, intervention/comparator label, and analysis assignment.
elements.reason: The number of reviewers involved in data extraction (one extractor plus one checker) is explicitly stated.

elements.quote: One reviewer extracted each record and a second reviewer checked eligibility classification, arm denominators, outcome timepoint, mean, standard deviation, direction of effect, intervention/comparator label, and analysis assignment.
elements.reason: The manuscript reports the independence arrangement: data were extracted by one reviewer and verified by a second (checking rather than fully independent duplicate extraction), and text_9 notes the kappa applies only to a paired verification subset, clarifying the independence status.

elements.quote: Disagreements were resolved by discussion, with senior clinical and methodological input from Zhirong Dai when needed.
elements.reason: Disagreement resolution process (discussion with senior adjudication) is described.
No processes for obtaining or confirming data from study investigators are reported anywhere in the retrieved evidence.
Machine prescreening is mentioned for screening, but no automation tools used specifically for data collection, nor their training/validation for extraction, are described.
Although Chinese databases were searched, no methods for translating non-English articles for data collection are reported.
No software or method for extracting data from figures is specified in the retrieved evidence.

elements.quote: When several pain timepoints were available, the closest clearly intra-procedural biopsy or sampling pain timepoint was selected. ... When a trial contributed more than one eligible active arm against a single inert control, active arms were combined before meta-analysis so that the shared control group was counted only once.
elements.reason: Decision rules for selecting among multiple timepoints and multiple reports/arms (including handling of duplicate publications in text_9) are described.

elements.quote: The primary outcome was pain during endometrial biopsy or endometrial sampling, measured on a 0-10 compatible visual analogue, numerical rating, or equivalent pain scale, with higher scores indicating worse pain... Secondary and supplementary outcomes included binary high-pain outcomes, pain at other procedure-related timepoints, need for additional analgesia, participant satisfaction or willingness to undergo repeat biopsy, procedure failure, and adverse events or complications.
elements.reason: All outcome domains are listed and defined, including scale, direction, and how safety outcomes would be handled.

elements.quote: Secondary and supplementary outcomes included binary high-pain outcomes, pain at other procedure-related timepoints, need for additional analgesia, participant satisfaction or willingness to undergo repeat biopsy, procedure failure, and adverse events or complications.
elements.reason: The primary outcome's time frame (during biopsy) is specified, but measurement time frames for most secondary outcomes are not explicitly defined beyond 'other procedure-related timepoints'.

elements.quote: For continuous pain outcomes, extraction prioritized pain during biopsy or sampling. When several pain timepoints were available, the closest clearly intra-procedural biopsy or sampling pain timepoint was selected.
elements.reason: The manuscript indicates that not all compatible results were sought; only the closest intra-procedural timepoint was collected for the primary outcome.

elements.quote: When several pain timepoints were available, the closest clearly intra-procedural biopsy or sampling pain timepoint was selected.
elements.reason: The selection rule for choosing among multiple compatible results is explicitly described; text_7 further specifies extractability criteria for the primary analysis.
No evidence of changes to outcome-domain inclusion, definitions, or importance with rationales is reported in the retrieved evidence.
No changes to processes for selecting results within outcome domains are reported in the retrieved evidence.

elements.quote: Certainty of evidence was assessed using the GRADE approach for outcomes prioritized for the Summary of Findings [10].
elements.reason: Prioritization of outcomes (pain during biopsy as primary, safety narrative) is evident, but an explicit rationale for prioritization is only implicit.

elements.quote: Extracted study-level fields included authorship, publication year, setting, country, design, sample size, eligibility criteria, biopsy device, procedural context, intervention details, comparator details, randomization and blinding information, registration or protocol availability, and funding or conflict-of-interest information when reported. Arm-level extraction captured the active intervention, dose or concentration, timing, route, co-interventions, comparator content, and number randomized or analyzed.
elements.reason: The methods comprehensively list and define all variables sought at study, arm, outcome, and analysis levels, including funding/conflict information and outcome-specific fields.

elements.quote: Trials reporting only medians and ranges were not converted into means and standard deviations for the main result because such conversion would require distributional assumptions. ... Somchit 2015 was not included because the reported variance values for pain during biopsy are implausibly small as standard deviations and are more consistent with standard errors or a reporting problem.
elements.reason: The manuscript explicitly describes assumptions and handling of missing or unclear information, e.g., refusing median-to-mean conversion requiring distributional assumptions and interpreting implausible variance values as possible standard errors.
No tool for determining which data items to collect is cited anywhere in the retrieved evidence; the data items appear to be author-defined, so this conditional requirement does not apply.

elements.quote: Risk of bias for randomized trials was assessed using the Cochrane RoB 2 framework at the outcome level
elements.reason: The tool (Cochrane RoB 2) is explicitly named and used for risk-of-bias assessment.

elements.quote: Particular attention was given to allocation concealment, participant and operator blinding, credibility of placebo or sham controls, post-randomization exclusions, completeness of pain-score reporting, and whether multiple pain timepoints created selective-reporting concerns.
elements.reason: Domains of concern are described, but the standard RoB 2 domains are not formally enumerated; the description is informal ('particular attention').

elements.quote: Study-level domain judgments and their contribution to the outcome-level GRADE assessment are provided in Supplementary Table S3.
elements.reason: Overall/domain-level judgments are reported (e.g., low risk vs some concerns in text_20) and documented in Supplementary Table S3.
No adaptations to the RoB 2 tool are reported; the standard framework appears to be used as-is.
No newly developed risk-of-bias tool is described; an established tool (RoB 2) was used.

elements.quote: RoB 2 judgments for the primary-analysis trials were made or checked by two reviewers and finalized by consensus.
elements.reason: Two reviewers assessed RoB independently/with consensus; text_9 adds disagreement resolution via discussion with senior input.
No evidence of contacting study investigators to obtain or confirm risk-of-bias information; no such process is reported.
No automation tools for risk-of-bias assessment are reported; machine prescreening applied to screening, not RoB assessment.

elements.quote: For continuous pain outcomes on a 0-10 compatible scale, the effect measure was the mean difference. ... For binary high-pain and adverse-event outcomes, the planned effect measure was the risk ratio with 95% confidence intervals.
elements.reason: Effect measures are specified for each outcome type: mean difference for continuous pain outcomes and risk ratio for binary high-pain and adverse-event outcomes.
No thresholds or ranges for interpreting the size of effects (e.g., what constitutes a clinically meaningful MD) and their rationale are reported in the retrieved evidence.

elements.quote: Scores reported on a 0-100 mm scale may be linearly expressed on a 0-10 scale when otherwise eligible, but the primary analysis did not use distributional conversions from medians, ranges, interquartile ranges, or ordinal categories.
elements.reason: Re-expression of 0-100 mm VAS scores onto the 0-10 scale is described, but the manuscript explicitly states other conversions (e.g., from medians or ordinal data) were not performed, so re-expression methods are only partially covered.
The choice of mean difference and risk ratio as effect measures is stated but no explicit justification for these choices is provided in the retrieved evidence.

elements.quote: To avoid mixing clinically different comparisons, we organized the evidence into three tiers. Tier 1 was the prespecified primary meta-analysis. It included inert-controlled randomized comparisons with extractable intra-procedural means and standard deviations. Tier 2 comprised sensitivity analyses... Tier 3 comprised narrative or tabulated contextual evidence.
elements.reason: The methods describe explicit processes and criteria for assigning studies to each synthesis: detailed eligibility criteria for the efficacy synthesis, additional criteria for the primary continuous meta-analysis, and a three-tier hierarchy (primary meta-analysis, sensitivity analyses, narrative/tabulated contextual evidence) applied before interpreting the pooled estimate. Data extraction (text_10) also states each record was classified as included in the primary analysis, summarized narratively, assigned to sensitivity analysis, or excluded.

elements.quote: Scores reported on a 0-100 mm scale may be linearly expressed on a 0-10 scale when otherwise eligible, but the primary analysis did not use distributional conversions from medians, ranges, interquartile ranges, or ordinal categories. Standard errors for study-specific mean differences were calculated from extracted arm-level sample sizes and standard deviations when not directly available.
elements.reason: The manuscript explicitly describes data preparation methods: handling of missing summary statistics (SEs calculated from arm-level n and SD), scale conversions (0-100 mm to 0-10), and explicit refusal to convert medians/ranges/ordinal data. Additional detail in text_10 (combining multiple active arms using sample-size weighted means and Cochrane Handbook SD formula) and text_30 (exclusion of studies with non-extractable or implausible variance data) further supports full reporting of data preparation methods.

Tables exist (e.g., Table 1 study characteristics, Table 2 Summary of Findings, supplementary tables), but no Methods text describes the tabular structures used to display results or the data included in them.

Figures are referenced (e.g., Supplementary Figure S5 exploratory mechanism-stratified forest plot, 'generated figures'), but no Methods section describes the graphical methods used to display results.
No evidence reports the basis for ordering or grouping studies within tables or graphs.

elements.quote: Supplementary Figure S5 exploratory mechanism-stratified forest plot
elements.reason: The only graphs referenced are standard types (forest plots, sensitivity plots); no non-standard graphs are indicated, so no rationale for non-standard graphs is required.

elements.quote: Analyses were conducted in R version 4.6.0. Random-effects meta-analysis, leave-one-out analysis, REML estimation, Hartung-Knapp-Sidik-Jonkman intervals, and prediction intervals used metafor 5.0-1 and meta 8.5-0.
elements.reason: Software and package versions for statistical synthesis are explicitly reported.

elements.quote: Trials outside the primary estimand or without extractable means and standard deviations were summarized narratively. This included trials reporting only ordinal or binary pain outcomes.
elements.reason: Alternative narrative/tabulated synthesis for non-poolable trials is described, with rationale given in text_7 (tiered evidence hierarchy) and text_34.

elements.quote: The conventional headline analysis used a DerSimonian-Laird random-effects model based on study-level mean differences and standard errors.
elements.reason: The random-effects model is reported; rationale (small number of studies, substantial heterogeneity, expected clinical heterogeneity) is provided.

elements.quote: For continuous pain outcomes on a 0-10 compatible scale, the effect measure was the mean difference... For binary high-pain and adverse-event outcomes, the planned effect measure was the risk ratio with 95% confidence intervals.
elements.reason: Statistical methods (effect measures, standard error calculation, pooling approach) are described.

elements.quote: Statistical heterogeneity was assessed using the Q statistic, tau-squared, and I-squared.
elements.reason: Methods to identify and quantify heterogeneity are explicitly reported.

elements.quote: The conventional headline analysis used a DerSimonian-Laird random-effects model... robustness was checked using restricted maximum likelihood random-effects estimation
elements.reason: Between-study variance estimators (DerSimonian-Laird primary; REML in sensitivity checks) are reported.

elements.quote: Hartung-Knapp-Sidik-Jonkman confidence intervals, and 95% prediction intervals
elements.reason: Method for calculating confidence intervals for summary effects (including HKSJ adjustment) is reported.

elements.quote: robustness was checked using restricted maximum likelihood random-effects estimation, Hartung-Knapp-Sidik-Jonkman confidence intervals, and 95% prediction intervals, and these checks were used to judge the uncertainty around the average effect.
elements.reason: Additional random-effects implementation details (REML, HKSJ, prediction intervals, leave-one-out) are reported.
No Bayesian meta-analysis was performed; all methods described are frequentist.
No method for handling statistical dependency among multiple estimates from the same study (e.g., multiple timepoints or arms) is described in the synthesis methods.

elements.quote: several clinically relevant studies could not be included in the continuous primary estimate because they reported medians, ranges, ordinal outcomes, binary high-pain thresholds, ambiguous variance values, or estimands outside the prespecified primary comparison.
elements.reason: Planned syntheses judged inappropriate (e.g., pooling non-extractable data) are identified with reasons; narrative summarization was used instead.

elements.quote: To explore clinical heterogeneity, we also generated an exploratory forest plot stratified by intervention mechanism: intrauterine local anesthetic, cervical topical anesthetic, mixed local anesthetic, and systemic COX-2 inhibition.
elements.reason: Methods to explore heterogeneity are explicitly described, including stratified exploratory forest plots, sensitivity analyses, and heterogeneity statistics (Q, tau-squared, I-squared).

elements.quote: an exploratory forest plot stratified by intervention mechanism: intrauterine local anesthetic, cervical topical anesthetic, mixed local anesthetic, and systemic COX-2 inhibition
elements.reason: The factor (intervention mechanism) and its levels are reported, but no expected direction of effect modification is stated; the authors only note heterogeneity was expected because mechanisms differ.

The manuscript does not report whether heterogeneity analyses used study-level variables, within-study contrasts, or both; stratification was by study-level intervention class but this distinction is not explicitly addressed.

elements.quote: Because class-specific groups were small, these estimates were descriptive; no formal test of subgroup differences or meta-regression was performed.
elements.reason: The method for comparing subgroup effects is reported: no formal statistical test was used; subgroup estimates were descriptive only.

elements.quote: Trials outside the primary estimand or without extractable means and standard deviations were summarized narratively. This included trials reporting only ordinal or binary pain outcomes.
elements.reason: Narrative summarization of non-pooled trials is described, but informal exploration of heterogeneity with specific factors and levels for these non-meta-analyzed studies is not described.

elements.quote: we also generated an exploratory forest plot stratified by intervention mechanism ... these estimates were descriptive; no formal test of subgroup differences or meta-regression was performed
elements.reason: The mechanism-stratified analysis is explicitly labeled 'exploratory' and descriptive, and the balanced-background-ibuprofen analysis is identified as 'not part of the primary estimand', distinguishing non-pre-specified analyses.

elements.quote: Additional sensitivity analyses included exclusion of high-risk-of-bias studies, exclusion of explicitly non-blinded or likely unmasked no-analgesic controls, restriction to placebo or saline controls, and an intervention-boundary analysis excluding the single systemic-only COX-2 inhibitor trial.
elements.reason: Methods describe multiple sensitivity analyses (leave-one-out, REML, HKSJ, prediction intervals, exclusions, balanced-background-ibuprofen), with results reported in text_22.
